name: East Anglia ONE North
subtitle: Offshore substation
location: Southern North Sea, off Suffolk, United Kingdom
role: HV & protection interface coordination · August 2026 – Present
intro: Connecting HV and protection interfaces, wiring documentation and multidisciplinary layout coordination for an offshore substation.
overview: East Anglia ONE North is an offshore wind development in the southern North Sea off the Suffolk coast, developed by East Anglia ONE North Ltd within ScottishPower Renewables’ East Anglia portfolio. It forms part of the East Anglia Hub and received development consent in March 2022. The founder’s work focuses on the offshore substation’s HV, protection and selected mechanical-system electrical interfaces.
note: 800MW is the wind farm capacity shown for this project. The founder’s involvement began in August 2026; responsibilities below are based on the founder’s October 2026 update.
facts: HV, protection and auxiliary system interfaces
work: FIM interface management
Manage and coordinate FIM interfaces for high-voltage and protection systems.
Aucotec wiring & interface diagrams
Create wiring connection and interface diagrams in Aucotec for HV and protection systems.
Structural & 3D layout coordination
Support the client on critical HV and protection system interfaces in coordination with structural engineering and 3D layout teams.
Mechanical-system electrical design
Develop electrical system designs for selected critical mechanical systems: the Oil Water Separator, Clean Water System, Condition Monitoring System and Main Crane System.
perspective: Clear wiring documentation and coordinated electrical, structural and spatial interfaces help teams resolve integration questions during design. This experience supports consulting scopes that connect HV and protection packages with the wider offshore substation.
sources: East Anglia ONE North project overview

name: Fengmiao I
subtitle: Offshore substation
role: HV commissioning lead / Project lead HV
intro: Connecting detailed engineering, equipment procurement and fabrication-yard delivery for a major offshore substation.
overview: Fengmiao I is a 495 MW offshore wind development off Taiwan’s west coast. Developed through a Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners fund, with Copenhagen Offshore Partners leading development, it reached financial close in March 2025. The planned wind farm comprises 33 Vestas 15 MW turbines, with construction completion targeted for the end of 2027 in the developer’s announcement.
note: 495 MW is the wind farm’s planned installed capacity. Its auction allocation was 500 MW of grid capacity; the founder’s CV describes the 500 MW offshore substation scope.
work: Engineering & procurement
Led the HV engineering package during detailed design, coordinating four engineers and multi-million-euro equipment procurement packages.
Installation & commissioning

Directed installation and commissioning activities for transformers, shunt reactors, earthing / auxiliary transformers and 66 kV / 220 kV GIS. Coordinated HV engineers and OEM specialists at the fabrication yard.
Protection & interfaces
Performed Siemens protection relay testing using Omicron equipment and coordinated technical, spatial and electrical interfaces between the engineering team and PTSC.
perspective: An offshore substation brings many separately procured packages into one electrical system. Equipment interfaces, protection requirements and test sequencing need to remain aligned as the design moves into installation and commissioning.
sources: Financial close and project configuration · 19 March 2025

name: Coastal Virginia
subtitle: Offshore substation
intro: Translating project requirements into structured acceptance testing for utility-scale offshore electrical infrastructure.
overview: Coastal Virginia Offshore Wind is Dominion Energy’s commercial offshore wind development off Virginia Beach. The US Bureau of Ocean Energy Management approved a configuration of 176 wind turbines and three offshore substations, with an estimated capacity of approximately 2,600 MW. Semco Maritime’s consortium announcement describes three 880 MW offshore substations forming the electrical backbone of the development.
note: The public project description uses approximately 2.6 GW. This replaces the rounded 2.7 GW figure in the previous website and founder’s CV.
work: Acceptance test procedures
Prepared Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) and Harbor Acceptance Testing (HAT) guidance for high-voltage equipment packages.
Standards alignment
Aligned the testing guidance with the applicable IEEE / IEC framework and the project’s owner / client requirements.
Package-level preparation

Focused on HV acceptance documentation as part of Semco Maritime’s engineering delivery. This experience is specific to testing preparation, rather than a claim of responsibility for the full wind farm.
perspective: For a multi-substation development, consistent acceptance documentation helps connect equipment-level verification with the wider commissioning programme. Clear requirements make the intended test scope easier for suppliers and site teams to interpret.

name: Formosa 4
subtitle: Offshore substation
intro: Establishing clear technical requirements and reviewing supplier proposals before equipment commitments are made.
overview: Formosa 4 is a 495 MW offshore wind project developed by Synera Renewable Energy off Miaoli County. The project website describes a site of approximately 58 km², with its nearest point around 20 km from shore. Its planned electrical infrastructure includes 500 MW offshore and onshore substations, with an intended connection to Taipower’s Fangli substation.
note: 495 MW refers to wind generation capacity; 500 MW refers to the stated substation capacities. These are different project ratings.
work: Employer’s Requirements
Authored Employer’s Requirements for the high-voltage infrastructure scope.
Tender evaluation
Assessed international equipment vendor proposals against engineering requirements.
Engineering compliance
Reviewed technical compliance within the tender process, bringing HV equipment knowledge into procurement-stage decisions.
perspective: Tender-stage choices set the technical basis for later design and delivery. Clear equipment requirements and a disciplined comparison of supplier proposals help expose gaps before packages advance into procurement.
sources: Project location, wind capacity and substation configuration

name: Greater Changhua 2b & 4
subtitle: Offshore substation
intro: Managing equipment documentation, technical variations and factory-to-yard interfaces across major HV packages.
overview: Greater Changhua 2b and 4 is Ørsted’s 920 MW offshore wind development, located 35–60 km off Taiwan’s Changhua coast. The project comprises 66 Siemens Gamesa 14 MW turbines. Ørsted reported completion of turbine installation in January 2026 and held a ceremony marking completion of major construction works in September 2026, with final commissioning activities still described in that announcement.
note: 920 MW is the published combined project rating. Milestones above are dated announcements, not a claim of current commercial operation.
work: HV package management
Managed design documentation, technical variations and contract compliance for transformers, GIS, EATs and busducts.
Factory acceptance testing
Led FAT activities with European equipment suppliers.
Fabrication-yard interfaces
Resolved spatial and technical design interfaces with the Seatrium fabrication yard in Singapore.
perspective: Factory acceptance and yard integration are closely linked. Equipment documentation, changes and physical interfaces need coordinated review so that packages remain compatible as they move from suppliers to the offshore platform.

name: Greater Changhua 1 & 2a
subtitle: Onshore substation
intro: Bringing OEM equipment, local EPC delivery and protection systems together at the onshore grid interface.
overview: Greater Changhua 1 and 2a is a 900 MW offshore wind development in Taiwan. Ørsted inaugurated the wind farms in April 2024 and reported that they were operating and fully connected to the grid. The developer’s milestone record notes onshore substation energization in February 2022 and first wind farm power in April 2022.
note: The founder’s experience described here concerns the onshore substation and grid integration scope, rather than the full offshore construction programme.
work: SAT / SIT integration
Managed integration interfaces between global OEMs and local EPC contractors during site acceptance and system integration testing.
Protection & energization
Troubleshot protection panels and supported substation energization into the 161 kV national grid switching station.
Cable-system integration
Directed installation and integration of a high-voltage cable culvert box control system.
perspective: Grid connection depends on more than individual equipment tests. Protection, controls and OEM / EPC interfaces must be considered together to prepare a substation for integrated testing and energization.

name: Mailiao Power Plant
subtitle: Power plant operation
intro: Practical experience with high-voltage asset maintenance, emergency repairs and transformer engineering in an operating industrial environment.
overview: Mai-Liao Power Corporation was established in 1996 by companies within the Formosa group. Its original independent power project comprised three 600 MW generating units, commissioned between 1999 and 2000, at the Mailiao industrial park in Yunlin County. This profile focuses on the founder’s 2020–2021 high-voltage operations and maintenance experience.
note: 1.8 GW describes the original three-unit project relevant to this experience. It is not a statement of the plant’s current operating capacity or the capacity of the wider industrial complex.
work: Operations & repairs
Supervised routine O&M and emergency grid repairs for 161 kV autotransformers and circuit breakers.
Protection & transformers
Programmed Siemens protection relay parameters and managed engineering rebuild work for 161 kV / 33 kV transformers.
Condition monitoring
Developed and deployed thermal-imaging analytics to identify early signs of CT / VT component failures.
perspective: Operating substations provide a direct view of maintainability, protection behaviour and equipment failure modes. That field experience informs how equipment and test requirements can be reviewed during new project delivery.
sources: Company history and original project configuration
